text:
maria.g: Heads-up — teaching folks through the sample app today and hit a startup hang when running the dockerized example with uvicorn+gunicorn.
kevin: can you paste the traceback or logs?
maria.g: nothing obvious in traceback, but app never returns from /health while container shows 100% CPU on one core. logs: `INFO: Started server process` then silence.
kevin: did you use the async client in module scope by any chance?
maria.g: yes, sampleapp/main.py creates an AsyncClient at import time and also wires an auth callback that does requests to our token endpoint.
oliver: ohhh. Sync token fetch inside async auth callback?
maria.g: the auth callback is currently sync because we reused our old helper: `def fetch_token(): time.sleep(0.1); return token` — so I think it's blocking the event loop during startup. we call it from httpx.Auth (sync) while AsyncClient starts.
kevin: that explains CPU spike. httpx tries to run sync auth in event loop thread and blocks. but why does uvicorn hang entirely? should still return after auth callback finishes.
maria.g: reproducible in container during startup — looks like we also trigger a retry/backoff loop because token endpoint times out in CI, so repeated blocking + retry prevents other tasks from progressing.
oliver: can you share a minimal repro? even a short script that imports AsyncClient with auth that calls time.sleep in auth hook will show it.
maria.g: repro gist: ```python
# repro.py
import time
from httpx import AsyncClient
class BlockAuth:
    def auth_flow(self, request):
        time.sleep(0.05)
        yield request
client = AsyncClient(auth=BlockAuth())
# import triggers no await but constructor does some setup
```
kevin: nice. short-term workaround: use anyio.to_thread.run_sync or run sync token fetch in ThreadPoolExecutor so it doesn't block loop. or make auth async: `async def fetch_token()` and use httpx.AsyncAuth interface.
maria.g: verified — wrapping token fetch with `await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(sync_fetch)` fixed startup and removed CPU spike.
oliver: for SDK we should: 1) document that sync auth hooks block event loop and recommend to use to_thread.run_sync, 2) provide an async-friendly auth helper in the Python SDK (like AsyncTokenAuth) that users can drop in, 3) detect obvious sync blocking patterns in our sample apps and replace them.
kevin: also consider catching accidental time.sleep in examples — maybe run a lint or unit test that runs sampleapp startup under asyncio and fails if import blocks >50ms.
maria.g: +1. Also flagged onboarding docs: our quickstart copy shows a naive `get_token()` helper that uses requests — we should change to aiohttp/httpx async example.
oliver: open ticket?
kevin: created an issue in SDK repo (#4123) with repro and proposed patch: add AsyncTokenAuth + update samples + doc note. tagging SDK owners.
maria.g: thanks — adding note for docs team to edit the quickstart. feels bad to block a live tutorial. :facepalm:
deploy-bot: Deployed patch branch kevin/sdk-async-auth-prop to staging for manual validation.
maria.g: verified on staging — health checks green now. thanks! :tada:
